newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run jumps on strength of crude rally.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run jumps on strength of crude rally.

text.p: European straight-run fuel oil prices leapt up on Monday as crude soared in value and residual oil once more became attractive to refiners, traders said.
A 25,000 tonne cargo of Scandinavian low sulphur straight-run loading 18-22 May was heard to have traded to a major in Europe for a price that would give a bid/offer range of $101/$103 fob.
Another seller in the undersupplied market said he had been inundated with bids but had held off selling until he could establish where crude would stabilise.
"At this crude level straight-run is much, much cheaper to refine," said one trader.
In the north Russian straight-run cargoes were thinly supplied and little discussed, though premia were believed to have widened on the back of crude's strength.
In the Mediterranean higher premia were sought but buying interest was limited, with only two Italian refiners needing material and most bunker outlets satisfied.
